sections.title: Who fills this in

fields.label: Filled in by
fields.help: your name, so we know whom to ask

fields.label: Date
fields.help: the day you filled it in, as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2026-10-26

fields.label: Notes to us
fields.help: anything we should know: where a value comes from, which values are estimates, what you want to learn from this coupon

sections.title: The coupon

fields.label: Units
fields.help: the unit system every number on this form is in: mm-MPa (mm, MPa and N), m-Pa (m, Pa and N), in-psi (in, psi and lbf) or in-ksi (in, ksi and lbf); the row labels are written for mm-MPa, so with another system read each unit as that system's. Results come back in the units you pick; our Abaqus and CalculiX decks are written in mm, MPa and N whatever you pick

fields.label: Test
fields.help: the kind of test: unnotched tension (a plain strip pulled), unnotched compression (a plain strip pushed), open-hole tension (a strip with a hole at its centre, pulled), in-plane shear (a strip of +45 and -45 plies only, pulled), three-point bending (a strip on two supports pushed down at midspan), four-point bending (pushed down at two lines), plate (a laminate held and loaded on regions you name, stated from the studio) or fibre tow tension (a resin-impregnated carbon fibre tow under ASTM D4018, stated and calculated from the studio, with no model); see Definitions, Tests

fields.label: Material code
fields.help: optional: a short code for the material in the coupon's name, capital letters and digits, X840PW in X840PW-UNT-L1; left blank, the code this material already has is reused, or a new one is derived from the library record (IM78552 for im7-8552) or numbered (M1, M2, ...) for your own constants

fields.label: Layup code
fields.help: optional: a short code for the stacking sequence, L1, L2 and so on; left blank, the code of this same stacking sequence is reused or the next free one is given

fields.label: Standard
fields.help: the test standard the specimen follows, from our list, or none for your own design. With a standard picked we check the coupon against each of its clauses a model can meet and report the deviations; see Definitions, Test standards

fields.label: Specimen
fields.help: the standard's specimen when it names more than one: for ASTM C1869, A (a 6 mm hole in a 36 mm wide strip), B (a 3 mm hole in a 10 mm wide strip) or other (a size of its Annex A1, reported as a variation); for ASTM D638, its Type I, II, III, IV or V of Fig. 1; blank otherwise

fields.label: Where the size comes from
fields.help: where the length, width and tabs come from: a standard, a drawing, or your own design

fields.label: Your Abaqus model of this coupon
fields.help: the name of your Abaqus model or job for this coupon, or not built yet

fields.label: Test data
fields.help: measured results we can compare with (a test report or a file name), or none

sections.title: Geometry: the coupon lies with its length along y, the direction it is pulled, pushed or spanned; lengths in the units stated above

fields.label: Length (mm)
fields.help: the whole coupon from end to end along the pull, tabs included, e.g. 250; for bending, the span plus the two overhangs

fields.label: Width (mm)
fields.help: across the coupon, e.g. 25

fields.label: Tab length (mm)
fields.help: how much of each end the grip holds, e.g. 56; 0 for no tabs, and then set Grip region to line. Required for the pulled and pushed tests; leave it blank for bending, which has supports instead of grips

sections.title: Dog-bone (unnotched tension only: a dumbbell, as ASTM D638 Fig. 1 draws it; leave the four rows blank for a straight strip)

fields.label: Narrow width (mm)
fields.help: the width of the narrow section at mid-length, W in ASTM D638, e.g. 13; the Width row above is then the overall width at the ends, WO

fields.label: Narrow length (mm)
fields.help: the length of the straight narrow section, L in ASTM D638, e.g. 57

fields.label: Fillet radius (mm)
fields.help: the radius of the fillet that joins the narrow section to the wider ends, tangent to the narrow section, R in ASTM D638, e.g. 76

fields.label: Outer radius (mm)
fields.help: only for a reverse curve, ASTM D638 Type IV: the second arc's radius, tangent to the wide end, RO, e.g. 25; blank when the fillet meets the full width at a corner

sections.title: Tabs and strain measurement (pulled and pushed tests; leave blank for bending and a plate)

fields.label: Tab thickness (mm)
fields.help: the thickness of each bonded tab, e.g. 1.5; leave the three tab rows blank when the coupon is gripped directly or through emery cloth. We draw and report the tabs; our model holds the gripped length rigidly

fields.label: Tab bevel angle (deg)
fields.help: the angle of the tab's end facing the gauge section, in degrees: 90 is a square end, 7 a long taper; ASTM D3039 takes 5 to 90

fields.label: Tab material
fields.help: what the tabs are made of, e.g. E-glass/epoxy at 45 degrees, or steel

fields.label: Strain measurement
fields.help: how the test reads strain along the coupon: an extensometer or a bonded strain gauge; ASTM D3039 needs it, since its minimum length counts the gauge length

fields.label: Strain measurement length (mm)
fields.help: the extensometer's gauge length or the strain gauge's active length, e.g. 25; it must fit between the grips

sections.title: Bending (three- and four-point bending only; ignored for the other tests)

fields.label: Support span (mm)
fields.help: the distance between the two support lines, e.g. 48, as the standard you follow sets it. The coupon lies across the supports with its length along y

fields.label: Overhang (mm)
fields.help: how far the coupon reaches past each support, so that Length = span + 2 overhang; 0 for a coupon that ends at its supports

fields.label: Loading span (mm)
fields.help: four-point bending only: the distance between the two loading noses, centred on the span, e.g. half the support span

sections.title: Open hole (open-hole tension, or a plate with a hole; ignored for the other tests)

fields.label: Hole diameter (mm)
fields.help: the diameter of the hole at the centre of the coupon, e.g. 6; on a plate the hole's ring becomes a region you can hold or load

fields.label: Nodes around the hole
fields.help: how many mesh points sit on the edge of the hole; a multiple of 4, at least 8. More points give a rounder hole and a sharper peak stress

fields.label: Element rings around the hole
fields.help: how many rings of elements surround the hole before the regular mesh starts; more rings give more detail near the hole

fields.label: Ring ratio
fields.help: how far the ringed region reaches from the hole's centre, in hole radii: 2 means a square reaching 2 radii out on each side; it must stay inside the width

fields.label: Ring growth
fields.help: how much thicker each ring is than the one inside it: 1.2 means 20% thicker, so the smallest elements sit at the edge of the hole, where stress changes fastest; 1 keeps every ring the same

sections.title: What the coupon is made of: plies of a composite, or one isotropic material such as a plastic

fields.label: Material kind
fields.help: plies: a laminate of plies, stated by the layup and a ply material below; isotropic: one material alike in every direction, such as a plastic or a metal sheet, stated by its thickness, E and nu here, with its name and source on the Own material rows, and no plies

fields.label: Thickness (mm)
fields.help: isotropic only: the coupon's thickness, e.g. 3.2

fields.label: Own material: E (MPa)
fields.help: isotropic only: Young's modulus, e.g. 3000 for a rigid plastic

fields.label: Own material: nu
fields.help: isotropic only: Poisson's ratio, above -1 and below 0.5, e.g. 0.35 for a plastic; no unit

sections.title: Layup, bottom ply first

fields.label: Ply 1 (bottom)
fields.help: the fibre angle of the bottom ply in degrees, measured from the coupon's length, the direction it is pulled: 0 = fibres along the pull, 90 = fibres across the width, 45 and -45 diagonal. Then one ply per row upward; leave the rest blank

fields.label: Ply 2
fields.help: the next ply up

fields.label: Symmetric
fields.help: yes: the plies listed are the lower half and are mirrored, so 0, 45, -45, 90 becomes 8 plies; no: the plies listed are the whole stack; required for plies

fields.label: Ply thickness (mm)
fields.help: the cured thickness of one ply, e.g. 0.127; leave blank only when the library material gives one (its Ply thickness column on the sheet Library materials)

sections.title: Material: pick one from our library, or give your own constants

fields.label: Library material
fields.help: pick a material by its id; the sheet Library materials lists each one with its constants and source, and once you pick one this cell shows its constants

fields.label: Own material: name
fields.help: the material's name as in your Abaqus model, no spaces, e.g. X840-Z60

fields.label: Own material: E1 (MPa)
fields.help: stiffness along the fibres (Young's modulus in direction 1)

fields.label: Own material: E2 (MPa)
fields.help: stiffness across the fibres, in the plane of the ply (direction 2)

fields.label: Own material: G12 (MPa)
fields.help: in-plane shear stiffness (shear modulus in the 1-2 plane)

fields.label: Own material: nu12
fields.help: Poisson's ratio: how much the ply narrows across the fibres when stretched along them, e.g. 0.3; no unit

fields.label: Own material: F1t (MPa)
fields.help: strength along the fibres in tension. Give all five strengths, or none: without them we predict no failure

fields.label: Own material: F1c (MPa)
fields.help: strength along the fibres in compression, as a positive number

fields.label: Own material: F2t (MPa)
fields.help: strength across the fibres in tension

fields.label: Own material: F2c (MPa)
fields.help: strength across the fibres in compression, as a positive number

fields.label: Own material: F6 (MPa)
fields.help: in-plane shear strength

fields.label: Own material: source
fields.help: where these numbers come from: the supplier's datasheet and its date, or a test report. They stay with this coupon and never go into our library

fields.label: G13 (MPa)
fields.help: out-of-plane shear stiffness in the plane of the fibres and the thickness, as in your Abaqus material (Lamina); required for plies. No measured value? For a tape use G13 = G12 and say so in the notes; see Definitions, Material

fields.label: G23 (MPa)
fields.help: out-of-plane shear stiffness across the fibres and the thickness, as in your Abaqus material (Lamina). Required for plies. No measured value? For a tape use G23 = E2 / 3 and say so in the notes; see Definitions, Material

sections.title: Failure criterion: which first-ply failure criterion we report

fields.label: Failure criterion
fields.help: all: every criterion the material allows (maximum stress and Tsai-Hill, and Tsai-Wu when f12* is given below); or one of them; or none. A criterion needs the material's strengths; see Definitions, First-ply failure

fields.label: Tsai-Wu interaction f12*
fields.help: the normalised interaction term of the Tsai-Wu criterion, a number between -1 and 1, neither included; required for Tsai-Wu; leave it blank otherwise, and Tsai-Wu is not reported

sections.title: Loading: the bottom grip is held, the top grip moves; in bending, the supports hold and the nose moves

fields.label: Loading type
fields.help: displacement: the top grip moves by the value, a length; force: a total force pulls or pushes the top grip. Bending takes displacement: the loading nose travels by the value

fields.label: Value (mm or N)
fields.help: the amount as a positive number, e.g. 1 mm or 10000 N; for compression we push, for the other tests we pull; in bending the nose pushes down by this travel

sections.title: Mesh: an element size, or your Abaqus mesh

fields.label: Element size (mm)
fields.help: the size of the small pieces (elements) the coupon is divided into for the calculation, e.g. 2. Smaller is finer: more detail near the grips and a hole, but slower. We put a row of nodes exactly on each tab line

fields.label: Your Abaqus mesh: elements across the width
fields.help: only if you already meshed this coupon in Abaqus: the number of elements across the width. Give this and the next two instead of an element size, and our mesh matches yours node for node

fields.label: Your Abaqus mesh: partition lines (mm)
fields.help: where your partition lines cross the length, measured from the bottom end, comma-separated, e.g. 56, 110, 140, 194

fields.label: Your Abaqus mesh: rows per segment
fields.help: how many rows of elements lie in each segment between those lines, from the bottom, so one more number than there are lines, e.g. 28, 27, 10, 27, 28

sections.title: Grips (ignored for bending, which rests on supports)

fields.label: Grip kind
fields.help: coupling: the gripped nodes at each end are tied to one reference point, held at the bottom and moved at the top, as in your Abaqus models; nodal: the gripped nodes themselves are held or moved

fields.label: Grip region
fields.help: tabs: every node on the tab is held; line: only the row of nodes at each end (use it when Tab length is 0)

sections.title: Names in your Abaqus model (optional: give them and our Abaqus file uses them)

fields.label: Abaqus name: part
fields.help: the part's name; leave all five blank and we use ours

fields.label: Abaqus name: instance
fields.help: the instance's name in the assembly, e.g. Coupon-1

fields.label: Abaqus name: material
fields.help: the material's name under Property, Material

fields.label: Abaqus name: layup
fields.help: the composite layup's name

fields.label: Abaqus name: section set
fields.help: the set the layup is assigned to

how_to: What this form is for. You describe one coupon test; from it we build the model in our engine, solve it, and send back a package: the document, our Abaqus deck of the same coupon, and the audit form on which you compare your Abaqus results with ours.

Fill in the yellow cells only. Rows marked 'required' must be given; the others have a default or may stay blank. The Units row says which units every number is in: mm, MPa and N unless you pick another system (m-Pa, in-psi or in-ksi); the results come back in the same units, and our Abaqus and CalculiX decks are written in mm, MPa and N whatever you pick. Every row says what it means beside it; the sheet Definitions explains each term with an example.

Directions: the coupon lies with its length along y, the direction it is pulled or pushed, and its width along x. Ply angles are measured from the coupon's length, the direction it is pulled, as ASTM D3039 counts them: 0 = fibres along the pull, 90 = fibres across the width. Our Abaqus deck carries this as a layup orientation whose direction 1 is global y, so its layer lines show the angles as you wrote them.
Layup: one ply per row, bottom ply first, angles in degrees. With Symmetric = yes, the plies you list are the lower half and are mirrored.

Material: either pick one from the sheet Library materials, or give your own constants with their source. Not both. G13 and G23 are needed in both cases, for the shell section of the Abaqus model; take them from your Abaqus material, or estimate them as the sheet Definitions says and write in the notes that they are estimates. If the library material has no strength in a column, we predict no failure; if it has no ply thickness, give one. A plastic, or any material alike in every direction, is Material kind = isotropic: give its thickness, E and nu, and its name and source on the Own material rows, and leave the plies, the ply material, G13 and G23 blank.
Failure criterion: all reports every criterion the material's strengths allow, maximum stress and Tsai-Hill, and Tsai-Wu too when you give its interaction term f12*; or pick one criterion, or none.

Mesh: give an element size and we divide the coupon so that a row of nodes sits on each tab line; or, when you already have an Abaqus model, give its mesh (elements across the width, the partition lines from the bottom, and the rows per segment) so that ours matches it node for node.

Dog-bone: for a dumbbell specimen, such as ASTM D638's, give the narrow section's width and length and the fillet radius (and Type IV's outer radius); Width and Length are then the overall sizes at the ends. Unnotched tension only; leave the rows blank for a straight strip. Open hole: the hole rows are read only for open-hole tension and for a plate with a hole. Bending: the span, overhang and loading span rows are read only for the two bending tests, which rest on two support lines instead of grips. Loading: give the amount; for compression we apply it as a push, and in bending the nose pushes down by it. A plate lists its supports and loads over named regions instead; it is stated from the studio.

Where we read results: at the centre of the coupon and just past the bottom tab; on an open-hole coupon, beside and above the hole and halfway to the tab. You do not enter these points: we place them from the geometry.

Standard: pick the test standard the specimen follows from the list, or none for your own design. With a standard picked we check the coupon against each of its clauses a model can meet, list every deviation with its clause, and list the clauses of the procedure (specimens, conditioning, speed, alignment, failure mode) as the laboratory's. ASTM D3039 also needs the strain measurement; ASTM C1869 needs its specimen, A, B or other; ASTM D638 needs its type, I to V. A deviation never stops the run, and we never say a model conforms to a test standard.
Names: if you give the names of your Abaqus part, instance, material, layup and section set, our deck opens in Abaqus/CAE with them.
Send the file back as it is. If something is missing or inconsistent, we send it back with every problem named.

terms.meaning: A test specimen: a flat strip of the laminate, held at both ends by grips and pulled or pushed along its length.
terms.example: A 250 x 25 mm strip with 56 mm tabs.

terms.meaning: Lay the coupon flat with its length running up the page. x runs across the width from the left edge (x = 0); y runs along the length from the bottom end (y = 0). The coupon is pulled or pushed along y.
terms.example: The centre of a 250 x 25 mm coupon is at x = 12.5, y = 125.

terms.meaning: A tab is the end region a grip holds. The tab line is where the tab ends and the free part of the coupon begins.
terms.example: With 56 mm tabs on a 250 mm coupon the tab lines are at y = 56 and y = 194.

terms.meaning: The free part between the tabs, where the coupon should fail and where results are read.

A coupon narrower in its middle than at its ends: a straight narrow section joined to the wide ends by fillets, so that it fails in the narrow section and not in the grips. The plastics tensile test, ASTM D638, uses it.
terms.example: ASTM D638 Type I: 13 mm wide over 57 mm, a 76 mm fillet, 19 mm wide at the ends.

terms.meaning: A plain strip pulled along its length. It gives the laminate's tensile stiffness and strength.
terms.example: ASTM D3039/D3039M for composites, and ASTM D638 for plastics on a dog-bone, both in our Standard list.

terms.meaning: A plain strip pushed along its length. It gives the compressive stiffness and strength. Our model is flat and in-plane, so it does not buckle.
terms.example: ASTM D6641 (not in our Standard list yet).

terms.meaning: A strip with a hole drilled through its centre, pulled. The hole concentrates the stress at its edge.
terms.example: ASTM D5766 for polymer composites (not in our Standard list yet); ASTM C1869 for ceramic composites, in our list, whose Specimen A is a 6 mm hole in a 36 mm wide strip (Table 1).

terms.meaning: A strip made of +45 and -45 plies only, pulled. The plies are loaded in shear, which gives the shear stiffness and strength.
terms.example: ASTM D3518 (not in our Standard list yet). Every ply +45 or -45, as many of each.

terms.meaning: A flat laminate held and loaded on regions you name: an edge, a tab, the ring of a hole, the whole face, or a box you draw on it. Each support says which directions it holds (and a travel, if it moves); each load is a force along a direction spread over its region, or a pressure on an area. Stated from the studio, which draws the regions; the Excel form has no rows for them.
terms.example: A square plate simply supported on its four edges under a pressure.

terms.meaning: A strip resting on two support lines, pushed down at midspan by a loading nose that moves by the value you give. It gives the flexural stiffness and strength; the outer plies carry most of the stress, the bottom ones in tension.
terms.example: ASTM D7264 procedure A (not in our Standard list yet).

terms.meaning: A strip on two support lines, pushed down by two loading noses centred on the span. Between the noses the moment is constant, so the failure is not under a nose.
terms.example: ASTM D7264 procedure B (not in our Standard list yet).

terms.meaning: The span is the distance between the support lines; the overhang is what reaches past each support (Length = span + 2 overhang); the loading span is the distance between the two noses of four-point bending.
terms.example: Span 48, overhang 6: a 60 mm coupon.

terms.meaning: The test method the specimen follows, picked from the list on the Standard row, or none for your own design. With a standard picked we check the coupon against each of its clauses a model can meet and say which are met. We hold the standard's values with their clause numbers, in our words; read the clauses in your own copy.
terms.example: ASTM D3039/D3039M-17 for unnotched tension.

terms.meaning: A size the standard names. ASTM C1869 names Specimen A, a 6 mm hole in a 36 mm wide strip (Table 1), and Specimen B, a 3 mm hole in a 10 mm wide strip (Table 2); other is a size of its Annex A1, reported as a variation (section 9.2.6).
terms.example: A.

terms.meaning: A requirement of the standard the coupon does not meet. The coupon still runs; the checklist and the document state the deviation with its clause. We never say a model conforms: the procedure (specimens, conditioning, speed, alignment, failure mode) is the laboratory's.
terms.example: D3039 Table 1: a 150 mm coupon that needs at least 187 mm.

terms.meaning: A size or value the standard suggests without requiring it, such as the sizes ASTM D3039 suggests for each class of laminate in its Table 2. A recommendation not followed is noted, not counted as a deviation.
How the test reads strain along the coupon: an extensometer, by its gauge length, or a bonded strain gauge, by its active length. ASTM D3039 counts the gauge length in its minimum length (Table 1).
terms.example: An extensometer of 25 mm.

terms.meaning: Bonded tabs: their thickness, the angle of their end (90 degrees is a square end), and what they are made of. We draw and report them; our model holds the gripped length rigidly and does not carry the tabs as material.
terms.example: 1.5 mm glass/epoxy tabs with a 7 degree bevel.

terms.meaning: One layer of the laminate: fibres in resin, all at one angle.

The direction of a ply's fibres, in degrees, measured from the coupon's length, the direction it is pulled, positive counterclockwise when you look down on the coupon. 0 = fibres along the pull, 90 = fibres across the width, 45 and -45 diagonal. Our Abaqus deck sets the layup's direction 1 along global y, so its layer lines carry these angles as written.
terms.example: If your own Abaqus model counts its angles from x, across the width, in the global axes, subtract 90 from every angle: 90, -45, 45, 0 becomes 0, 45, -45, 90.

terms.meaning: List the plies from the bottom face up, in the order you would lay them on the tool.
The stack is mirrored about its middle. With Symmetric = yes, list only the lower half.
The cured thickness of one ply.
A material whose constants we hold with their source and page. Pick its id; the sheet Library materials lists each one with its constants, and the row on the form shows the one you picked.
terms.example: im7-8552: IM7/8552 carbon/epoxy tape, NCAMP.

terms.term: Empty cell on the sheet Library materials
terms.meaning: The source does not give that value. With no strength we cannot predict when a ply fails, so we leave failure out; with no ply thickness, give one on the form.
Your own constants, with where they come from. They stay with this coupon and never go into our library.

A material alike in every direction, such as a plastic or a metal sheet: it has no plies, and two constants state it, Young's modulus E and Poisson's ratio nu (the shear modulus is E / (2 (1 + nu))). Our deck writes it as Abaqus's isotropic Elastic and a homogeneous shell section of the thickness you give.
terms.example: A rigid plastic: E = 3000 MPa, nu = 0.35, 3.2 mm thick.

terms.meaning: The ply's own directions: 1 along the fibres, 2 across the fibres in the plane of the ply, 3 through the thickness.
Stiffness (Young's modulus) along the fibres (E1) and across them (E2).
terms.example: IM7/8552 in our library: E1 = 162,096 MPa, E2 = 8,963 MPa.

terms.meaning: In-plane shear stiffness: how the ply resists shear in its own plane.
Poisson's ratio: how much the ply narrows across the fibres when it is stretched along them. No unit.

terms.term: Strengths F1t, F1c, F2t, F2c, F6
terms.meaning: The stress at which a ply fails: along the fibres in tension (F1t) and compression (F1c), across the fibres in tension (F2t) and compression (F2c), and in in-plane shear (F6). Compression as a positive number. Give all five or none.

The rule that says when a ply has failed, from its stresses and strengths. Maximum stress: a ply fails when one stress reaches its strength. Tsai-Hill and Tsai-Wu: the stresses are combined, so no single one governs. All reports every criterion the material's strengths allow.
terms.example: all, our default; or one of maximum stress, tsai-hill, tsai-wu; or none.

terms.meaning: The interaction term of the Tsai-Wu criterion, normalised, between -1 and 1 (neither included). Tsai-Wu needs it; the other criteria do not.
terms.example: Leave it blank and Tsai-Wu is not reported.

terms.meaning: Out-of-plane shear stiffness: G13 in the plane that holds the fibres and the thickness, G23 across the fibres and the thickness. Abaqus needs them for the shell section (its Lamina material asks for them). Our own solver does not use them, so they do not change our results for a thin coupon pulled or pushed.
terms.example: No measured value: for a tape the usual estimate is G13 = G12 and G23 = E2 / 3 (the ply taken as the same in every direction across the fibres, with nu23 = 0.5; MIL-HDBK-17-3F, section 10.2.4.1). For a woven fabric there is no reliable estimate: ask the supplier. Either way, write in the notes which values are estimates.

terms.meaning: Where your own constants come from.
terms.example: The supplier's datasheet and its date, or a test report and its number.

terms.meaning: The top grip moves by a set distance; the bottom grip is held. We report the force it takes.
terms.example: 1 mm.

terms.meaning: A set total force pulls or pushes the top grip; the bottom grip is held. We report how far it moves.
The gripped nodes at each end are tied to one reference point, which moves like a rigid grip: held at the bottom, moved at the top. This is how your Abaqus models grip the coupon.
The gripped nodes are held or moved directly, without a reference point.
tabs: every node on the tab is held. line: only the row of nodes at each end.
terms.example: Use line when Tab length is 0.

terms.meaning: For the calculation the coupon is divided into small four-sided pieces called elements; their corners are the nodes. The stress is worked out in every element. The whole set of elements is the mesh.
terms.example: A 250 x 20 mm coupon with 2 mm elements has 10 across and 125 along: 1,250 elements.

terms.meaning: About how long an element's side is. We divide the width, and each part of the length, into whole numbers of elements of about this size, with a row of nodes exactly on each tab line.
terms.example: 2 mm, our default; 1 mm for a finer check.

terms.meaning: Smaller elements. They show more detail where the stress changes quickly (at the end of a tab, around a hole) and take longer to solve. In the middle of a plain coupon the stress is the same everywhere, so a finer mesh changes nothing there.

If you have meshed this coupon in Abaqus, give its seeds instead of an element size: elements across the width, the partition lines from the bottom, and the rows in each segment. Our mesh is then the same as yours node for node, and the results can be compared element by element.

Nodes around the hole: points on the hole's edge. Element rings: rings of elements around the hole. Ring ratio: how far the ringed region reaches, in hole radii. Ring growth: how much thicker each ring is than the one inside it.
terms.example: Our defaults: 32 nodes, 6 rings, ratio 2, growth 1.2.

terms.meaning: The force the grip needs to make the movement you gave.
The load at which the first ply anywhere in the coupon reaches its strength, by the criterion you chose on the Failure criterion row; given as a fraction of your load, with the place and the ply.
terms.example: 0.93: the first ply fails at 93% of a 1 mm pull.

terms.meaning: At the centre of the coupon and just past the bottom tab; on an open-hole coupon, beside and above the hole and halfway to the tab. We place these points from the geometry; you do not enter them.
Material code, test code and layup code. Test codes: UNT unnotched tension, UNC unnotched compression, OHT open-hole tension, IPS in-plane shear.
terms.example: X840PW-UNT-L1: X840 plain weave, unnotched tension, layup 1.

profiles.title: Tensile properties of polymer matrix composites
profiles.edition_note: read from the D3039/D3039M-17 copy licensed to UC San Diego; the publisher lists D3039/D3039M-17(2025), a reapproval, as active (that its text is unchanged is UNVERIFIED)
profiles.systems: SI and inch-pound, each used on its own (§1.2)

classes.label: 0° unidirectional
classes.note: bonded tabs with a 7° or a 90° bevel

classes.label: balanced and symmetric
classes.note: gripped through emery cloth without bonded tabs; Table 2 gives no grip length, so the tab length stays yours to state

requirements.text: The material is a polymer-matrix composite reinforced by high-modulus fibres.
The laminate is balanced and symmetric about the direction of the pull: a −θ ply for every +θ ply, and the stack a mirror image about its mid-plane.
The coupon has a constant rectangular cross-section.
The length is at least the gripped length, plus twice the width, plus the gauge length of the strain measurement (we read the gripped length as both grips together).
Bonded tabs are bevelled at 5° to 90°, both included.
The width suggested for the laminate's class.
The overall length suggested for the laminate's class.
The laminate thickness suggested for the laminate's class.
The tab length suggested for the laminate's class.
The tab thickness suggested for the laminate's class.
The tab bevel suggested for the laminate's class.
An extensometer's gauge length lies between 10 and 50 mm [0.5 and 2.0 in].
A bonded strain gauge's active length is at least 3 mm [0.125 in]; 6 mm [0.25 in] suits most materials.
Off-axis plies soften the free edges, so the strength and stiffness of an angle-ply laminate can read low.
The specimen's width is within ±1 % of its width.
The specimen's thickness is within ±4 % of its thickness.
The specimen lies flat under light finger pressure.
Bonded tabs match in thickness within ±1 % and are feathered into the coupon without damaging it.
Width and thickness are measured at three places in the gauge section, and the area is their average width times their average thickness.
At least five specimens are tested per condition.
The conditioning is reported; without one, the specimens are reported as unconditioned, moisture unknown.
The strain rate gives failure in 1 to 10 minutes: 0.01 per minute in strain control, or 2 mm/min [0.05 in/min] of the head as a start.
Bending is checked with back-to-back transducers on at least one specimen per sample at 2000 microstrain; above 3 % the strains of both faces are averaged.
The load train's alignment is checked; good practice keeps bending to 3 to 5 % above 1000 microstrain.
Each failure is recorded with the three-part code of the failure type, area and location.
When many specimens fail within one width of a tab or grip, the gripping is re-examined.

profiles.title: Tensile properties of plastics
profiles.edition_note: read from the D638-22 copy the founder supplied, the active edition; every clause held here is the same in D638-14
profiles.systems: SI; the inch-pound values are for information only (§1.5)

variants.label: Type I: 13 mm wide over 57 mm, for material 7 mm thick or less (the preferred type)
variants.note: the overall width and length are the least allowed; the grips leave the distance D between them; the extensometer spans the gage length G

variants.label: Type II: 6 mm wide over 57 mm, for material 7 mm thick or less that will not break in Type I's narrow section
variants.note: the overall width and length are the least allowed; the grips leave the distance D between them; the extensometer spans the gage length G

variants.label: Type III: 19 mm wide over 57 mm, for material over 7 mm and up to 14 mm thick
variants.note: the overall width and length are the least allowed; the grips leave the distance D between them; the extensometer spans the gage length G

variants.label: Type IV: 6 mm wide over 33 mm with two radii, for material 4 mm thick or less, nonrigid or compared across rigidity
variants.note: the overall width and length are the least allowed; the grips leave the distance D between them; the extensometer spans the gage length G

variants.label: Type V: 3.18 mm wide over 9.53 mm, for material 4 mm thick or less when little is at hand
variants.note: the overall width and length are the least allowed; the grips leave the distance D between them; the extensometer spans the gage length G

requirements.text: The material is a plastic, unreinforced or reinforced. A resin-matrix composite reinforced by oriented fibres stiffer than 20 GPa is tested by ASTM D3039/D3039M instead.
The specimen is at most 14 mm thick; thicker material is machined down to 14 mm.
The specimen is a dumbbell of Fig. 1: a narrow section joined to wider ends by fillets.
The thickness lies in the type's range: up to 7 mm for Types I and II, over 7 mm and up to 14 mm for Type III, up to 4 mm for Types IV and V.
A reinforced composite, a highly orthotropic laminate included, is tested as Type I.
The narrow section's width W is the type's, within its band.
The narrow section's length L is the type's, within its band.
The fillet radius R is the type's, within its band.
Type IV's outer radius RO is 25 mm within its band; the other types have none.
The overall width WO is at least the type's, and at most that plus its tolerance (our reading of the plus tolerance).
The overall length LO is at least the type's; longer is allowed.
The distance D between the grips is the type's, within 5 mm. With self-tightening grips on a highly extensible polymer, D may follow the grips, kept the same once chosen (note J).
An extensometer spans the full gage length G, within its band; for referee tests it must.
A molded specimen, and a Type I or II specimen where possible, is 3.2 mm thick within 0.4 mm.
Type I is the preferred specimen where material 7 mm thick or less is at hand.
Sheet or film thinner than 1.0 mm is better tested by ASTM D882.
The SI values are the standard; the inch-pound values in parentheses are for information only. A coupon stated in inches is held to the millimetres, converted exactly.
A material suspected of anisotropy is tested with specimens cut along and across its suspected direction, five of each.
The width at the centre is W to 0.10 mm less, any narrowing gradual and equal on both sides.
A Type IV die's narrow section is 6.00 mm wide within 0.05 mm.
Surfaces are free of visible flaws; machining marks are filed and sanded away along the long axis; molded flash is removed.
Gage marks are drawn in wax crayon or India ink, never scratched, punched or pressed in.
The grips are fixed or self-aligning, hold the specimen without slipping, and align its long axis with the pull.
A modulus is measured with an extensometer of Class B-2 or better (ASTM E83) that records continuously; elongation up to 20 % needs at least Class C.
At least five specimens per sample; for an anisotropic material, five along and five across its principal direction.
A specimen that breaks at a flaw or outside the narrow section is discarded and retested.
The speed is the lowest in Table 1 for the specimen and rigidity that breaks it in 0.5 to 5 minutes: 5 mm/min (±25 %) is the lowest for rigid and semirigid Types I to IV, 1 mm/min for Type V.
Specimens are conditioned by Procedure A of ASTM D618 and tested in the same atmosphere.
Width and thickness are measured to 0.025 mm at the centre and within 5 mm of each end of the gage length.
The separation of the jaws is never used for the modulus or the elongation.
The toe of the curve is compensated unless it is the material's own response.
The tensile strength is the greatest force over the average original cross-section in the gage length, to three significant figures.
The modulus is the slope of the initial straight part of the curve over the average original cross-section; with no straight part, a secant modulus at a stated strain.

Poisson's ratio is measured at 5 mm/min after a preload under 5 N, to at least 0.5 % strain, with a transverse extensometer across the width; with no straight part, over 0.05 % to 0.25 % axial strain.

profiles.title: Open-hole tensile strength of fibre-reinforced advanced ceramic composites
profiles.edition_note: read from the C1869-18 (reapproved 2023) copy licensed to UC San Diego

variants.label: Specimen A: a 6 mm hole in a 36 mm wide strip
variants.note: the least length and grip length; longer is allowed

variants.label: Specimen B: a 3 mm hole in a 10 mm wide strip
variants.note: the least length and grip length; longer is allowed

requirements.text: The material is a ceramic matrix composite with continuous fibres.
The laminate is usually balanced and symmetric in two dimensions; another architecture is allowed and described in the report (§9.2.5).
The hole of the named specimen: 6.0 mm ± 0.2 mm for A, 3.0 mm ± 0.1 mm for B.
The width of the named specimen: 36 mm ± 0.5 mm for A, 10 mm ± 0.2 mm for B.
The width is at least 6 hole diameters for A and 3 for B; a hole under 4 mm in another size takes at most 30 % of the width.
The overall length is at least 120 mm for A and 60 mm for B.
The gauge length between the grips is at least 60 mm for A and 30 mm for B.
Each grip section is at least 30 mm long for A and 15 mm for B.
The thickness lies between 2 and 10 mm, both included.
The hole is centred within ±0.5 mm across the width and ±2 mm along the length.
A hole or strip of another size than A or B is reported as a variation.
The nominal thickness is 3 mm.
The hole diameter is nominally 2 thicknesses for A and 1 for B.
The gauge length is 10 hole diameters or more.
In a size other than A or B, a hole above 4 mm takes a width above 5 diameters, and a hole above 5 mm at least 6.
An extensometer spans at least three hole diameters, centred over the hole.
A bonded strain gauge along the coupon is at least 9 mm long.
The specimen holds the hole's circularity (±0.2 mm for A, ±0.1 mm for B), a uniform width (±0.5 mm for A, ±0.2 mm for B, and ±2 %) and the gauge length within ±2 mm.
The hole is drilled undersize and reamed to its diameter without delaminating the material.
The width is measured at the hole and 10 mm either side, the thickness at eight points, the hole at two diameters 90° apart, and the gauge length.
At least five valid specimens are tested.
Only a failure through the centre hole is valid: lateral, angled or multi-mode at the gauge middle.
The load train bends an alignment specimen by at most 5 %, and a gauged specimen by less than 10 %.
Displacement control, at a rate that breaks the specimen in 5 to 10 seconds.
Unnotched specimens of the same geometry are tested to compare the open-hole strength with.
Each failed specimen is examined and the fracture described, or the report says it was not.

profiles.title: Tensile properties of continuous-filament carbon and graphite fibre tows
profiles.edition_note: read from the D4018-23 copy licensed to UC San Diego

requirements.text: A continuous-filament carbon or graphite yarn, roving or tow, impregnated with resin and consolidated before it is pulled.
A gauge length of 150 mm ± 5 mm between the tabs, or between the grips of an untabbed specimen.
At least four valid specimens tested for strength.
At least four valid specimens tested for modulus, the same four as for strength or another four.
Several fibre bundles combined into one specimen only for a tow of 3000 filaments or fewer, the bundles combined before impregnation.
A consolidated resin able to strain at least twice as far as the fibre.
The forces for the chord modulus read at the strains Table 2 gives for the product's typical strain at failure.
A mass-per-unit-length specimen of sized fibre at least 1 m long.
A testing machine speed of at most 250 mm/min.
A uniform impregnation, typically 35 % to 60 % resin by weight.
The density measured on desized or unsized fibre.
A sized fibre's density is corrected for its sizing by k_c, found from ten paired tests; no correction is needed when sized and desized results differ by less than 1.0 %.
Each specimen's failure recorded by its type, area and location.
When a significant fraction of the failures lies within one specimen width of a tab or grip, re-examine the tabs, their adhesive, the grips, their pressure and their alignment.
A testing machine verified to ASTM E4 at the largest expected force, its force recorded together with the extensometer's elongation.
An extensometer and recorder of ASTM E83 Class B-2.
Masses on an analytical balance to ±0.0002 g; lengths to ±2 mm.
The density by ASTM D3800 Method A (Archimedes) or by D70 or D5550 (pycnometer).
Conditioning and the test atmosphere by the fibre's moisture adsorption: no conditioning below 0.5 % by weight at 23 °C and 90 % relative humidity, 24 h at 23 °C and 50 % relative humidity above it.
The impregnated strand held under tension while it consolidates, and cured in an oven held within ±10 °C.
A preload no larger than Table 1 gives, found from the expected modulus and the fibre's area (the planning loads below).
The specimen centred in the jaws and aligned with the load.
Fuzzy, curved, uneven or otherwise flawed specimens rejected unless they represent the material.
A flawed or suspect specimen replaced or retested, slippage and breaks in the tabs or at the extensometer counted as such, every value recorded.

sections.title: The fibre tow

fields.label: Fibre
fields.help: the fibre as its maker names it, with its filament count and sizing, e.g. T700SC-12000-50C; it identifies the samples tested (§13.1.3.1)

fields.label: Fibre type
fields.help: carbon or graphite, the fibres D4018 covers (§1.1); other for any other fibre, which lies outside it

fields.label: Lot or spool
fields.help: the lot, spool or batch the samples came from, for traceability (§13.1.3.1)

fields.label: Filaments per bundle
fields.help: the filament count of one bundle, e.g. 12000 for a 12K tow

fields.label: Bundles per specimen
fields.help: how many bundles were combined into one specimen: 1, or more only for a tow of 3000 filaments or fewer (§8.3)

sections.title: Mass per unit length and density (§8.1, §8.2, §12.1, §12.2)

fields.label: Mass per unit length (g/m)
fields.help: the sized fibre's mass per unit length, e.g. 0.800, or blank to compute it from the MUL specimen's mass and length (Eq 1)

fields.label: MUL specimen mass (g)
fields.help: the mass of the length of sized fibre weighed, e.g. 0.8012

fields.label: MUL specimen length (m)
fields.help: the length weighed, at least 1 m (§8.1), e.g. 1.000

fields.label: Density measured on
fields.help: the fibre the density was measured on: desized or unsized fibre is preferred (§4.3), and a sized fibre's density is corrected by k_c (§12.2.2)

fields.label: Measured density (g/cm³)
fields.help: the density measured on that fibre, e.g. 1.80

fields.label: Sizing correction k_c (g/cm³)
fields.help: for a sized fibre only: the correction found from ten paired tests of sized and desized fibre (§12.2.2), or blank for none

sections.title: The impregnated strand (§10.3, §12.3.1)

fields.label: Resin
fields.help: the resin and its hardener, e.g. a bisphenol A epoxy with diethyltoluene diamine (§13.1.3.5)

fields.label: Resin strain to failure (microstrain)
fields.help: the consolidated resin's strain to failure, at least twice the fibre's (§4.5), e.g. 50000

fields.label: Impregnation apparatus
fields.help: how the fibre was impregnated, e.g. a dip bath and a die (§13.1.3.5)

fields.label: Consolidation and cure
fields.help: the cure cycle, held under tension, e.g. 2 h at 120 °C (§13.1.3.5)

fields.label: Impregnated mass per unit length (g/m)
fields.help: MUL_i, the impregnated and consolidated strand's mass per unit length, for the resin content (Eq 3), or give the resin content instead

fields.label: Resin content (% by weight)
fields.help: the resin content when it was measured another way, or blank when MUL_i is given

sections.title: The tensile test (§8.3, §11.3)

fields.label: Gauge length (mm)
fields.help: the free length between the tabs, or between the grips of an untabbed specimen: 150 mm ± 5 mm (§8.3)

fields.label: Tabs
fields.help: the tabs on the ends, or none for a specimen gripped directly (§6.1.3)

fields.label: Machine speed (mm/min)
fields.help: the crosshead speed, at most 250 mm/min (§11.3.2)

fields.label: Testing machine and extensometer
fields.help: the tensile testing apparatus (§13.1.3.6)

fields.label: Test facility
fields.help: where the tests were run (§13.1.3.3)

fields.label: Typical strain at failure (microstrain)
fields.help: the product's typical strain at failure, e.g. 21000 for 2.1 %: it sets the chord strains (Table 2) and the largest preload (Table 1)

fields.label: Chord lower strain (microstrain)
fields.help: the strain the force P_l was read at, or blank for Table 2's

fields.label: Chord upper strain (microstrain)
fields.help: the strain the force P_u was read at, or blank for Table 2's

sections.title: Datasheet values, for the planning loads

fields.label: Datasheet strength (MPa)
fields.help: the fibre's tensile strength on its datasheet, e.g. 4900: the force to expect at failure

fields.label: Datasheet modulus (GPa)
fields.help: the fibre's tensile modulus on its datasheet, e.g. 230: the preload and the chord forces to expect

specimen_fields.label: Maximum force (N)
specimen_fields.help: P, the largest force before failure; blank for a specimen tested for modulus only

specimen_fields.label: Force at lower strain (N)
specimen_fields.help: P_l, read at the chord's lower strain; blank for strength only

specimen_fields.label: Force at upper strain (N)
specimen_fields.help: P_u, read at the chord's upper strain; blank for strength only

specimen_fields.label: Failure code
specimen_fields.help: the three letters of Fig. 1, the failure's type, area and location, e.g. LGM

specimen_fields.label: Status
specimen_fields.help: valid, or rejected with the reason in the note (§11.3.12): a rejected specimen is listed, not counted

specimen_fields.label: Note
specimen_fields.help: why it was rejected, or what was atypical about its failure (§13.1.3.8)

area.W: within one width of the grip or tab
